answer:
The Collatz-type map is

\[
T(n)=
\begin{cases}
n/2, & n \text{ even}\\
3n+1, & n \text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

To find starts that reach 10 after exactly three applications, reverse the map from 10.

Preimages of 10:
- \(2\cdot 10=20\)
- \(\frac{10-1}{3}=3\), since \(3\) is odd and \(3(3)+1=10\)

So
\[
T^{-1}(10)=\{20,3\}.
\]

Preimages of \(\{20,3\}\):
\[
T^{-1}(20)=\{40\}, \qquad T^{-1}(3)=\{6\}.
\]
Thus
\[
T^{-2}(10)=\{40,6\}.
\]

Preimages of \(\{40,6\}\):
\[
T^{-1}(40)=\{80,13\},
\]
since
\[
40=2\cdot 20 \quad \text{and} \quad 40=3(13)+1,
\]
and
\[
T^{-1}(6)=\{12\}.
\]
Thus
\[
T^{-3}(10)=\{80,13,12\}.
\]

Now verify forward:

\[
80\to 40\to 20\to 10,
\]

\[
13\to 40\to 20\to 10,
\]

\[
12\to 6\to 3\to 10.
\]

In each case, 10 is first reached on the third application.

\[
\boxed{12,\ 13,\ 80}
\]

are all positive starts that first reach 10 after exactly three applications.
